answer: The market elder seals the weigh beam at dawn, and every sack of salt is weighed on it at each oasis before it may be sold. A vertex sack weighed on a home beam fails the seal: at the canyon of the weighing the beam must balance exactly as the elder left it, and a home beam always tips light. Buying false salt means bribing the elder, forging a season of weighings and paying 11,300, while the onyx seal on the beam is broken if it is touched, so a sack whose weight was never measured is poured out.
